brief: LCX Services sources all new companies and contacts from Apollo. Saved audience, geography, size, buying-signal, credit and qualification constraints apply to automatic discovery and manual searches. Websites provide qualification evidence only. Each qualified buyer receives one evidence-based service route; every email requires human approval.

geography.guidance: The owner, 2026-10-06: "Everywhere allowed" -- every country except those whose law needs consent before a cold business email: Canada (CASL), Germany and Austria (UWG), Italy, the same set as LCX Clipping. A company is left out only on evidence: Wikidata says its only country is one of them, or the city it was found in is. english_markets earns half the priority_market bonus (the US, the UK, India and the UAE, enrichment.reveal_countries, earn all of it) because the email and the deck are in English; it never leaves anyone out. unpayable_countries (2026-10-07, the owner's decision that day): sanctioned countries LCX cannot invoice, left out by the payable_country gate: Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Syria and Cuba.

wikidata.note: listed on a stock exchange: ordinary corporates the class and industry queries miss
industry: cosmetics, clothing, food, beverages, consumer electronics, jewellery, furniture, e-commerce
retail chain, department store chain, supermarket chain, fashion house, online shop
bank, insurance company, asset management company
film production company, television production company, animation studio, advertising agency

audiences_guidance: Who buys which of the 18 services on docs/LCX Services.pdf, where they are found (tools/discover_lcx_services.py) and who to write to there (contact_roles, the titles Apollo is searched for, best first). Every email offers every service; the audience decides who is found, what the lead says it fits (why_fit, Pitch first) and audience_fit in the rubric: 1.0 where the sheet's services fit directly, 0.5 where the sale is slower (banks and insurers, attractions). corporate_teams (2026-10-07) is the owner's "normal corporates": any industry, 201-5,000 people, for the training, onboarding and explainer services. wikidata entries match a class (P31), an industry (P452) or a stock-exchange listing (P414); osm entries are OpenStreetMap tag pairs; the Apollo searches are in apollo_discovery. site_words (2026-10-07, scoring v4) are the words a business of that audience uses about itself on its own home page, which earn buyer_confirmed; size_bands are its sweet spot and the bands either side of it for buyer_size, in people, US dollars of revenue (assets for banks, pupils for schools).

discovery.guidance: Apollo-only discovery using audiences, country restrictions, size bands and buying signals. Historical source records remain evidence.

osm_discovery.guidance: OpenStreetMap's Overpass API, the endpoints tried in turn (the main one did not answer from the office on 2026-10-06; a mirror did). Each run takes discovery.osm.cities_per_run of these cities, a different few each ISO week, and asks each audience's tags within radius_m of the centre, for places that publish a website or an email address. Coverage follows the map's volunteers: on 2026-10-06 London had about 1,400 cafes with a website or address, Mumbai 26. Cities in English-speaking business markets only, since the email and the deck are in English; add a city here and it joins the rotation. Data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL, recorded on each lead it found.

rubric.label: The business is the buyer it was filed as, in its own words
rubric.guidance: Full credit when the company's own website (its home-page title, description or About text) uses at least two of its audience's words (audiences[].site_words): a hotel says rooms, suites or book direct, a school admissions, curriculum or IB, a developer apartments, villas or off-plan, a bank loans, mortgages or credit union. Half credit for one such word, or when a directory that sorts companies by what they are says so: Wikidata's class or industry, an OpenStreetMap tag, the FDIC bank register. That half stands when the site was read and says nothing either way, and for a mid-size company (corporate_teams) from any source, since any employer that size is the audience unless the wrong-buyer check says otherwise. No credit when only Apollo's keyword search says so and the company's own site does not back it up (its 'retailers' search returned OpenAI, Coinbase, CNET and IT-services firms), or when the site that answers is not this company's (Afribank's domain now serves an internet exchange). The heaviest weight, like international_ip_experience for the production houses: it separates a real buyer from a mislabelled one, and it is never unknown, because every lead carries a source label. Set by tools/lcx_judge.py on every chain run; the words it matched are on the lead (metadata.lcx_judgement). ADDED 2026-10-07 (scoring v4), replacing 'established', which was 1.0 on all 593 Wikidata leads and 762 of 768 Apollo rows and so told nobody apart.

rubric.label: Big enough to pay, small enough that one cold email reaches the person who decides (per buyer type)
rubric.guidance: Full credit inside the audience's sweet spot (audiences[].size_bands): mid-size companies 200-5,000 people or $20M-$1B revenue; banks and insurers 100-5,000 people, $20M-$2B, or $1-10bn of assets; retailers and hotels 20-5,000 people or $5M-$1B; studios and agencies 11-200 people or $1-50M; cafes, salons and independent shops 2-50 people, or several locations named on their own site; brands, developers, publishers, attractions and schools 20-1,000 people or $5-500M (schools also 300-3,000 pupils). Half credit in the band next to the sweet spot on either side, for one independent premises with a website, or for a company known only from Apollo's search band (a filter, not a measurement). No credit outside both bands: above them is a procurement process, below them there is no budget. The first measure that applies wins: FDIC assets, revenue, headcount (pupils for a school), the OpenStreetMap premises, Apollo's band. Unknown when no source measures the company: left out of the score (JSON null), not 0, so the score is out of the other 75 points; this mostly affects schools, attractions, hotels and developers that Wikidata gives no headcount. Set by tools/lcx_judge.py. REPLACES right_size (15) 2026-10-07: right_size scored 'Wikidata has no headcount' as 0 on 176 leads and had the production houses' team-page rule (2-20 named staff) written into 131 LCX leads by the site pass; a new key name keeps both stale values out.

rubric.label: Already pays for content: video and Instagram accounts it links to
rubric.guidance: Full credit for a video account (YouTube, TikTok or Vimeo) plus at least one more of those or Instagram, linked from the company's own website or listed for it on Wikidata or OpenStreetMap. Half credit for exactly one of them. No credit when the site was read and links none of them: Facebook, X or LinkedIn alone earn nothing, because that is not where paid video lives. Unknown (left out, not 0) while the website has not been read, or refuses the website reader (robots.txt, a dead domain), and no directory lists an account: about 29% of sites refuse, and leaving this out stops 20 points from measuring whether robots.txt let us in. A directory's listing can only raise the value. Why: LCX sells cheaper video, UGC and reels, and a company that already posts is the buyer our AI content makes cheaper; it weighs less than confirmation and size because a brand can be a good buyer before it has started. A lead is shortlisted automatically only once this is known (auto_shortlist.require_assessed). Set by tools/lcx_judge.py. ADDED 2026-10-07.

rubric.label: How directly the 18 services fit this kind of buyer (what to pitch first; every email still offers all 18)
rubric.guidance: From the owner's audience table (audiences[].fit), unchanged: 1.0 brands, retailers, real estate, hotels and short stays, publishers, studios and agencies, schools, mid-size companies, cafes, salons and gyms, independent shops; 0.5 banks and insurers, and attractions, where the sale is slower (vendor reviews and tenders). Written at discovery and rewritten by tools/lcx_judge.py from the lead's audience on every chain run, so a person's change of audience is picked up. LOWERED 2026-10-07 from 20 to 15: a slow-sale audience then costs 7.5 points, enough to order equal leads, never enough to exclude a strong one.

rubric.label: Named decision-maker identified and reachable
rubric.guidance: Set by the tools, never by hand. Full credit for a named person with their own address: a person in a target role whom Apollo has verified, or a named personal address on the company's own site. Half credit for a business inbox the company publishes (info@, hello@) on OpenStreetMap, on Wikidata or on its own site (tools/enrich_lcx_services.py, enrich_contacts). No credit while there is nobody. Only 10, the share the production houses give reach (10 of 110): whether a lead can be drafted is decided by the shortlist rule (someone the drafter will write to, a named person for banks and mid-size companies), not by these points, so reach no longer drowns fit. LOWERED 2026-10-07 from 50.

score_modifiers.label: BONUS: a reason to buy now (hiring trainers or content people, just raised money, opening or launching)
score_modifiers.guidance: Full credit when Apollo's signal search found the company hiring for training and onboarding, or for content and video, right now, hiring marketing staff for a launch (developers, hotels), or raising money in the last 90 days, once the company's own site has been read and is theirs; before that it earns half. Half credit for hiring frontline staff (sales and service, stores) once the site has been read, since many of those hiring are software firms taking on account executives, and for a launch or opening phrase in its own words ('now open', 'pre-launch', 'admissions open', 'we're hiring'; judge.trigger_phrases). It fades: an Apollo signal is worth half after 60 days and nothing after 120. Cancelled for a company the wrong-buyer check marks 1.0, because a staffing firm's or a training company's hiring is its product. Rare, so a bonus whose absence costs nothing, unlike a 30-point criterion that would be 0 for every Wikidata, FDIC and OpenStreetMap lead. ADDED 2026-10-07 at +8: enough to carry a directory-label lead of the right size with an inbox in a priority market over the line (64 to 72), never enough to rescue a wrong type.

score_modifiers.label: BONUS: LCX's own markets (US, UK, India, UAE), half for other English-speaking markets
score_modifiers.guidance: Full credit for a business based in the US, the UK, India or the UAE (enrichment.reveal_countries), LCX's first markets and the only countries Apollo reveals are paid for. Half credit in another English-speaking business market (geography.english_markets). No credit in any other allowed country; absent when the country is unknown. Small and additive, like india_diaspora_affinity for the production houses: it orders equal leads and never shortlists one on its own. REPLACES english_market (+4) 2026-10-07: the same size, but full credit now goes only to the four markets LCX sells to first.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: not a buyer of this (software firm, staffing agency, competitor, university, charity, investor, public body, vendor to the industry)
score_modifiers.guidance: 1.0 (the full -50) on clear evidence in the company's name, its page title or its domain, or when it describes itself plainly anywhere on its site ('a non-profit', 'registered charity', 'venture capital', 'hedge fund', 'staffing agency', 'online courses', 'corporate training', 'AI video studio'). The kinds: software or SaaS vendors, IT-services firms and payment or till providers included; staffing, recruitment and outsourcing firms (their job posts are their clients'); e-learning, training and AI-content competitors (NIIT, Coursera, FranklinCovey, Hero Vired); universities, seminaries and business schools filed as anything but a school; charities, associations, societies and institutes; investment firms, holding companies, lessors and ratings agencies; government bodies, .gov and .mil domains included; agencies and software sold to the audience itself (a Shopify agency filed as a brand, hotel software filed as a hotel); B2B suppliers (OEM, private label, ingredients). 0.5 (-25) when the same word appears only in the description, or for a borderline type: asset managers, marketplaces and distributors, liquor stores and drinks distributors filed as brands, commercial property, REITs and lenders filed as developers, news and media titles filed as brands or retailers, consultancies and law firms filed as mid-size companies, a .org domain on a company audience, a non-profit publisher or attraction. Schools are exempt from the non-profit, college, institute and academy tests, because an Indian 'Public School' is private. A bank's legal form is not a non-profit: 'National Association', 'Savings and Loan Association', 'Building Society', 'Credit Union' and 'Institution for Savings' are taken out before matching. The words are in judge.wrong_buyer and the other judge lists, and the phrase that matched is shown on the lead (metadata.lcx_judgement.wrong_buyer) so a reviewer can overrule it. -50, like client_work_dominance but sized to bite with a margin: a 1.0 lead with everything else perfect and both bonuses scores 62, eight points under the line, while a 0.5 is a warning a strong lead survives. ADDED 2026-10-07.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: too big to answer a cold email, or part of a large group
score_modifiers.guidance: 1.0 (-50) for revenue of $2-10B, more than 20,000 people, more than $50bn of assets, a brand's page on its group's domain (courtyard.marriott.com), the company's own words 'is now part of' or 'was acquired by', or, once fetched, a Wikidata parent organisation of more than 5,000 people or on the majors list. 0.5 (-25) for revenue of $1-2B, 5,001-20,000 people outside mid-size companies, a listed company with revenue over $500M, its own words 'one of the largest', 'part of the ... group', 'a subsidiary of', 'investor relations' or 'Fortune 500', or an OpenStreetMap premises whose website is one page of a chain's site. The highest value found wins. Like revenue_above_cap for the production houses: companies this size buy through procurement and have their own studios, and a 1.0 can never cross the line however perfect the rest. Anything bigger (over 50,000 people or $10B), and the named majors, is left out by the not_major gate instead. ADDED 2026-10-07.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: the company's own website is not in English (the email and the deck are)
score_modifiers.guidance: 1.0 (-15) when the home page's title and description are not in English: more than 30% of the letters are not Latin (Chinese, Japanese, Cyrillic, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai, Greek, Hebrew, Korean), or at least 3 common words of another language appear and outnumber the English ones two to one. 0 when the text reads as English. Absent when the site has not been read or the text is too short to tell (the About paragraph is tried then). A soft penalty, so a strong lead still passes, which keeps the owner's rule that language never leaves anyone out. An English cold email to a company that works in another language is rarely read: Zeeman, Gina Tricot, Clas Ohlson and Appart'City all sat in the shortlist of 2026-10-07. ADDED 2026-10-07.

gates.label: Not in a country where cold business email needs consent
gates.guidance: Fires only on confirmed evidence of a country in geography.disallowed_countries (CA, DE, AT, IT; the owner's 2026-10-06 'Everywhere allowed'). Unknown always passes. Written at discovery, and rewritten by tools/lcx_judge.py on every chain run from the same country the priority_market bonus uses: 'disallowed', 'unpayable' (the next gate) or 'allowed', absent when the country is unknown. Unchanged 2026-10-07; the harvest already drops these countries.

gates.label: Not in a sanctioned country LCX cannot invoice
gates.guidance: Fires only on evidence: the company's country is in geography.unpayable_countries (Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba), or, when no country is known, its domain ends .ru, .by, .ir or .su (judge.unpayable_tlds). 'Everywhere allowed' was about consent law, not payment. The same input as country_allowed, another value. ADDED 2026-10-07 (the owner's decision that day): 28 leads then, among them Bank of Russia, Rot Front, Citilink and Melnitsa Animation. Gates never archive a shortlisted lead, so the 3 already shortlisted (iConText, WeiT Media, VID) are only listed for a decision.

gates.label: Not a major, a major's named brand, or a giant
gates.guidance: Fires on any of: the domain or the name is on the curated majors list (judge.majors: each group's own domains and its named brands, such as Marriott's Courtyard, LVMH's Belmond or Merlin's Legoland); more than 50,000 people; revenue of $10B or more; more than $100bn of assets; once fetched, a Wikidata parent organisation on the list. The production houses exclude majors and their named subsidiaries with a gate, and this mirrors it: a major's hotel, park or brand buys through the group. Unknown always passes. Written by tools/lcx_judge.py (true or false). TIGHTENED 2026-10-07 from not_giant, 'over 100,000 people' (the owner's decision that day: over 50,000 people or $10B revenue, plus the named majors): 63 leads then, 55 by the list (Belmond, Fenty Beauty, Kylie Cosmetics, Zappos, both Legolands, Universal Studios Singapore, 1 Hotels, Emaar, Blackstone, AKQA...) and 8 giants (OpenAI, the NBA...).

gates.label: Not adult, gambling, tobacco or weapons, and not a site taken over by gambling spam
gates.guidance: Fires only on evidence in the company's name, page title or description: adult or porn words, casino, betting, gambling, slot-spam words, tobacco, vaping, firearms or ammunition (judge.unsafe_words); or the whole name is on judge.brand_risk_names (Vixen Media, bet365, Philip Morris, Smith & Wesson...); or, once fetched, its Wikidata class or industry is one of judge.unsafe_classes. These are a brand risk for TVF, and a domain that now serves gambling spam is not the company it was. Unknown always passes. ADDED 2026-10-07 (the owner's decision that day): 13 leads then, among them guns.com, Sturm Ruger, Private Media Group, and a school, a music park and a drinks firm whose sites now carry slot or togel spam.

gates.label: The company's domain still resolves and is not a parked or default page
gates.guidance: Fires only on evidence: the site pass found the domain does not resolve on two reads at least 7 days apart (metadata.dead_since, then a later read that also failed), or the home page is a parked or server-default page (an Apache or Ubuntu default page, 'It works', 'Index of', a domain for sale, an account suspended; judge.parked_titles). A robots.txt refusal, a timeout or a server error never fires it, as with the production houses' is_active gate. Unknown always passes. ADDED 2026-10-07.

gates.label: Some way to reach them: a website or an address
gates.guidance: Fires only on an explicit false. The harvest stages nothing without a website or a published address, so this is a guard.

auto_shortlist.guidance: The owner, 2026-10-07: shortlist automatically above 70, only with a usable contact and a read site. A lead in To review is shortlisted by the last step of the promote chain (sql/14_auto_shortlist.sql) when all three hold: its score is strictly above min_score; it has a contact the drafter will actually write to (require_contact: the same contact_rank test tools/outreach.py drafts by), and for banks and mid-size companies (named_contact_for) that contact is a named person, not an info@ inbox; and its content_activity has been assessed (require_assessed), meaning its site was read or a directory lists its accounts, so a lead scored on the few points known is never shortlisted before anyone has read its site. 70 is where the production houses' principle holds: the basics alone (a directory label, the right size, a full-fit audience, an inbox and a priority market score 64, 69 with a named person) stay out, and one real signal from the company carries a lead over (its own words confirming the audience 79, one video or Instagram account 74, a strong buying trigger 72). A lead over the line that fails the contact or site test stays in To review and is shortlisted on the first chain run after it gets one; one nobody can be written to waits for the Apollo reveal (enrichment.score_over) instead, and is never drafted. Shortlisting sends nothing: every draft still needs a person's approval. Leads at or below the line stay in To review, where a person can shortlist one by hand. RAISED 2026-10-07 from 55, which a lead with an address and nothing else could cross. require_site_read (2026-10-08): the company's own site was looked at (tools/lcx_judge.py's lcx_judgement.site_checked: its own words read, or its pages read and none a bot wall); a directory listing its accounts is not enough. The owner: shortlist only 'with a read site'.

wrong_buyer.label: competitor: e-learning, training or AI content

judge.guidance: The word lists tools/lcx_judge.py reads to set the inputs above from what is stored on each lead: its name and domain, its discovery record (Wikidata, Apollo, the FDIC register, OpenStreetMap) and the site pass's home-page title, description and About text. Change a word here, then run tools/gen_segment_sql.py lcx-services and apply sql/03f; the next chain run judges every lead again. Each entry is a word or phrase, matched as a whole word in upper or lower case; brackets and | work as in a regular expression for variants ('universit(y|ies)'), except several_locations, which matches anywhere. The *_names lists match the whole company name once Inc, Ltd, LLC, Group, plc, Corp, Co or Holdings is taken off, so 'Beacon Hill School' is not the staffing firm Beacon Hill and 'Kforce Inc' is. wrong_buyer rules: where 'any' scores the value wherever the words appear (plain self-descriptions such as 'a non-profit' or 'venture capital'); 'nt' scores it in the name or page title and at most half in the description or About text; 'title' counts only in the name or title (so 'university' in a biotech description is not evidence). exempt audiences skip a rule, only audiences are the ones it applies to (a lead not yet placed in an audience is checked by every rule), per_audience changes its value. software: full in the name or title for every audience but studios and agencies; in the description full for mid-size companies (half for the bare word 'software') and half for the rest; banks only on bank_words, at half. majors: each group's own domains (the name before .com or .co.uk) and its named brands, a stop-gap until the Wikidata and Apollo parent fields are fetched for every lead. too_big and not_major hold the size lines in people and US dollars. retired_inputs are removed from every lead's scoring inputs on each run. Set enabled to false to stop the judge (the chain then scores whatever inputs are stored). ADDED 2026-10-07 (scoring v4): the lists tested that day on the 2,402 live leads. 2026-10-08 (review): majors domains with a dot are a full registered domain (paramount.com), for names that are also common words; a bare name matches any ending. A name that only reads like a major's brand is too_big's -50, not the not_major gate, and a fund owning a stake never archives. Credit unions are not associations, so banks are out of the .org rule. unsafe_classes 'tobacco' skips Wikidata's standard retail class 'food, beverages or tobacco predominating', which every supermarket carries (Elvi, 2026-10-08).

enrichment.senior_titles: (founder|owner|ceo|chief executive|chief marketing|chief commercial|chief operating|chief people|(?<!vice )president|managing director|general manager|principal|head of school|head teacher|headmaster|headmistress)
enrichment.guidance: Apollo supplies new contacts in the target roles. Existing score, geographic and site-verification restrictions and credit caps apply. Websites are read only for qualification evidence.

sources.name: Apollo.io company search (weekly, inside the credit cap)
sources.detail: tools/discover_lcx_services.py --source apollo: mid-size companies with their websites, by audience, size and country, the ones hiring for content, training or store staff now and the recently funded first. 1 credit a page of 100.

sources.name: Apollo.io search (by hand)
sources.detail: The Apollo search page, for adding a lead by hand. Saving a person reveals them: 1 credit each.

self_exclusion.guidance: TVF and its affiliates never enter the lead pool, from any source. Domains match on the host or a subdomain, name patterns as whole words.

sender.name: LCX
sender.title: Business Development
sender.postal_address: Contagious Online Media Network Pvt Ltd. 702, 7th Floor, A Wing, Fortune Terraces, Opp. Citi Mall, New Link Rd, Andheri West, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400053
sender.guidance: Sender name, title and company for the shared sign-off. The company is the project's own (LCX), so one personal profile title works in every project and the company is never written into a person's title (the owner's review, 2026-10-13, point 10: no short-form titles in the sign-off). Whoever approves an email signs it with their own name and title (send_from approver); name LCX and title Business Development are the canonical form a draft is stored in. The address is retained as an optional footer field and omitted from the email footer (owner, 2026-10-09). The sending address comes from the connected Gmail account.

send_window.guidance: Owner, 2026-10-12: "I want you to send mails to the sender's time region between 10 to 10:30AM and that must be randmized not like all mail going at 10:15 some must be going at 10:17 some at 10:13 and so on after approval implement it". Each approved email goes out at its own random second between start and end on its RECIPIENT's clock (10:00 in Mumbai is 05:30 in London, too early to be read), drawn when it is approved and shown in Approved as "Goes out", with the time in India beside it. Where the recipient is comes from what the lead holds -- the person's own Apollo record, the company's state or city, a phone's area code, its country -- and the reason is kept on the email (tools/send_window.py). Monday to Friday on the recipient's clock (weekdays_only): an approval after today's window, or at a weekend, takes the next weekday's. An email whose window passes unsent (the server down, its address at its daily limit) moves to the next window at a new random time, never later the same day. Never two emails from one address closer than min_gap_seconds; never one sooner than min_lead_seconds after its approval. To send on the sender's clock instead (every email 10:00-10:30 India time) set timezone_of to "sender"; to switch the window off set enabled to false -- the stored times are cleared and approvals go out as soon as they can, as before. docs/runbook.md, "Goes out". A lead that names no place at all goes at New York's 10:00 (fallback_timezone): LCX Services pitches American and British companies first.

outreach.subject_max_words_guidance: The owner, 2026-10-13: "subject for all emails for all services should be less than 5 or equal to 5 words". Every rendered subject is checked against this (tools/draft_render.capped_subject): one over it uses its template's subject_fallback, and one still over it is not drafted, so a longer subject never ships. "Re:" in front of a follow-up is not counted.

footer.guidance: The owner's review, 2026-10-13, point 10: the title line reads "<title>, LCX" with the company from sender.company. The owner, 2026-10-13: the opt-out line is removed from every project's footer ("remove the last line from every single service"); any reply that is not neutral still stops all mail to that address. No postal address (owner, 2026-10-09). Edited in Outreach -> Footer; templates end with {{footer}}.

outreach.default_cc_guidance: The owner, 2026-10-22: "add a feature to cc someone from the software itself. Make default cc to the email amritanshv@lightscameraexperiment.com and obvio make a toggle to switch that off". Every email of this project is copied to these addresses unless the person approving it switches that off in the email (the CC toggle) or changes the list. The list an email is approved with is the one it goes out with (outreach.cc, sql/39, frozen at approval): changing this default never changes an email already approved. A reply from one of these addresses is not taken for the recipient's reply. [] copies nobody by default.

greeting.guidance: The owner's review, 2026-10-13, point 8: never "Hi there". {{greeting_line}} (an opener) is "Hello <first name>," and "I trust you are well." when a person is named (tools/draft_render.greeting_person: the contact's own first name, never a show or company name), else "Hello,". {{greeting}} (a follow-up) is the first line alone. {{first_name}} is the only field these lines take. greeting_fallback stays for the drafts written with v1 and v2.

Reel Forge.subject: One video, many reels
Reel Forge.problem: Most long-form videos get their attention in the week they are released, and then sit in the archive.
Reel Forge.solution: Reel Forge cuts long form videos into reels and distributes them across 5 to 10 Instagram pages, turning work you already own into a new format that reaches more people.

Airbnb / Property Content.subject: Your property photos, in motion
Airbnb / Property Content.problem: Most rooms and homes are still chosen from photos, which show the space but not what it feels like to be there.
Airbnb / Property Content.solution: Airbnb / Property Content turns the property photos you already have into cinematic reels, carousels and home tours.

AI VFX + Animation.subject: Bigger scenes, same footage
AI VFX + Animation.problem: Ambitious scenes are often cut at the budget stage, because the location, the set or the effects cost more than the production can carry.
AI VFX + Animation.solution: AI VFX + Animation makes the footage you have already shot cinematic, with AI environments and effects added afterwards.

Audiobooks and Audio Web Shows.subject: Your backlist, as audio shows
Audiobooks and Audio Web Shows.problem: Many titles on a publisher's list never get an audio edition, because a full production is hard to justify one book at a time.
Audiobooks and Audio Web Shows.solution: With Audiobooks and Audio Web Shows, we adapt books into audio shows, and the writers keep the rights and the revenue.

AI Video for Brands.subject: Campaign videos without the shoot
AI Video for Brands.problem: Every launch and campaign needs new video, and each one usually means booking another shoot.
AI Video for Brands.solution: AI Video for Brands produces product, ad and campaign videos without separate shoots.

studios_agencies.problem: Every client campaign needs new video, and each one usually means booking another shoot.

AI Real Estate Visualisation.subject: Walkthroughs before the first brick
AI Real Estate Visualisation.problem: Selling before construction means asking buyers to commit to a home they can only picture from drawings and floor plans.
AI Real Estate Visualisation.solution: AI Real Estate Visualisation turns your blueprints into realistic visuals and walkthroughs, so buyers can see the home before construction starts.

Explainer Videos.subject: One video, fewer questions
Explainer Videos.problem: When a product or service takes a conversation to explain, every new customer, recruit and partner needs that same conversation.
Explainer Videos.solution: With Explainer Videos, complex products, services and concepts are explained visually, so the explanation is made once and can be shared wherever it is needed.

financial_services.problem: Insurance and financial products usually take a conversation to explain, and every new customer needs that same conversation.

Shop Display Videos.subject: What's on your store screens?
Shop Display Videos.problem: In-store screens often play the same loop for months, while the products and offers around them keep changing.
Shop Display Videos.solution: With Shop Display Videos, your store screens show content made for your current collections, offers and promotions.

AI UGC Product Videos.subject: Your brand's own AI creator
AI UGC Product Videos.problem: Keeping a brand page supplied with regular product content usually depends on creators being available.
AI UGC Product Videos.solution: With AI UGC Product Videos, AI influencers create recurring product content on your brand's own page.

AI Podcasts / Audio Content.subject: Your products, as a conversation
AI Podcasts / Audio Content.problem: Many products need more explaining than an advert or a brochure has room for.
AI Podcasts / Audio Content.solution: AI Podcasts / Audio Content creates conversations between AI characters about your products and your brand, in a format customers can listen to.

financial_services.problem: Financial products usually need more explaining than an advert or a brochure has room for.
financial_services.solution: AI Podcasts / Audio Content creates conversations between AI characters about your products and financial services, in a format customers can listen to.

Virtual Tours for Schools.subject: Field trips without the bus
Virtual Tours for Schools.problem: The places a syllabus covers, from space and the ocean to ancient civilisations, are ones a school trip can rarely reach.
Virtual Tours for Schools.solution: With Virtual Tours for Schools, your students go on virtual field trips to space, the ocean, ancient civilisations and landmarks, from the classroom.

AI Reality Experiences.subject: A new reason to visit
AI Reality Experiences.problem: Giving visitors a reason to come back, or to bring friends next time, usually means adding something new to experience.
AI Reality Experiences.solution: With AI Reality Experiences, we build immersive VR experiences and games for your visitors, without the cost of a new physical build.

Creator × Brand Marketplace.subject: Finding the right micro influencers
Creator × Brand Marketplace.problem: Finding nano and micro influencers who suit a brand often takes longer than running the campaign itself.
Creator × Brand Marketplace.solution: Creator × Brand Marketplace is a platform where you can discover nano and micro influencers and run campaigns with them.

Local Business Tech and Automation.subject: Less admin behind the counter
Local Business Tech and Automation.problem: In many cafes, salons and gyms, bookings, billing and follow ups sit in different places, and some get missed.
Local Business Tech and Automation.solution: Local Business Tech and Automation sets up billing, bookings, WhatsApp follow ups and dashboards for your business.

AI Business Assistant.subject: Ask your business a question
AI Business Assistant.problem: Getting a straight answer on today's sales, open tasks or stock usually means waiting for a report or asking someone to pull the numbers.
AI Business Assistant.solution: AI Business Assistant gives you on demand answers on sales, tasks and inventory.

AI Simulations for Training.subject: Rehearse before the real customer
AI Simulations for Training.problem: New sales and service staff usually learn the difficult conversations on real customers, because there is nowhere safe to practise first.
AI Simulations for Training.solution: With AI Simulations for Training, your sales and customer facing teams work through real world scenarios that test and score them before they meet a customer.

AI Fashion Stylist.subject: A mirror that completes outfits
AI Fashion Stylist.problem: In the changing room a shopper is usually deciding on one piece, while the rest of the outfit stays on the shop floor.
AI Fashion Stylist.solution: AI Fashion Stylist is an AI mirror near your changing rooms that completes the look from your own store stock.

AI Onboarding Employee.subject: The same training, every hire
AI Onboarding Employee.problem: Every new hire needs the same induction, and how well each one is trained often depends on who had the time to train them.
AI Onboarding Employee.solution: AI Onboarding Employee is a digital trainer that teaches, tests and scores your new hires across 10 to 15 parameters, so every new joiner gets the same induction.

generated_pitch.guidance: The owner's review of the LCX Services emails, 2026-10-13 (template lcx_services_problem_v3): problem first, then the solution, then who we are, then one small ask; ONE service per email, the lead's lead service (lead_service below, tagged by tools/lcx_judge.py). service_copy holds, for each of the 18 services in the deck's order, its subject (at most five words, with a hook, never the company's name, never "18 things"), the fixed problem line and the fixed solution line, with by_audience variants where the buyer reads differently (banks, studios). A signal_problems line replaces a service's problem only while its Apollo hiring signal is fresh (scoring_inputs.buying_trigger above 0 and the judge's trigger evidence is the signal itself); raising money is a reason to write, never a problem, and the email never mentions it. The model (Groq, no retention) writes {{problem}} (problem_words) and {{solution}} (solution_words) for the one service from tools/draft_render.lcxs_facts v3: the audience label, the company's own site words when tools/lcx_judge.py found the site readable and theirs (an about page that is opening hours, terms, cookies, region pickers, codes, delivery offers, disclaimers or gift guides is left out: about_page_junk), the fresh signal as a reason_phrases phrase (never Apollo's wording), the accounts it posts on, and the service with its deck line (service_lines) and its problem hint. It is called only when there is something of theirs to write from (own words or a fresh signal); otherwise, and when it fails twice, both lines come from service_copy word for word. Its leash is tools/llm.py LCXS_SYSTEM v3 and check_lcxs: no metrics about them, no names, no dash of any kind, the service named exactly once, no other service, no number that is not in the deck line. An answer of no_fit holds the draft as Check service. default_pitch is kept for the v2 drafts' plain pitch. Three requests a minute keeps inside Groq's free plan. enabled false: every draft takes the fixed lines.

templates.subject: {{service_subject}}
templates.guidance: The owner's review of the LCX Services emails, 2026-10-13 (points 1, 4, 6 to 12). Problem first: the subject is the lead service's own (service_copy, at most five words with a hook); the greeting is "Hello <first name>," with "I trust you are well." or "Hello," (outreach.greeting); {{problem}} and {{solution}} are the two lines for the ONE lead service, written by the model (generated_pitch) or, when it is not called or fails twice, service_copy's fixed lines word for word; then who we are, in the deck's own words, with the deck attached; then one small ask; then the footer. {{company}} is the company as a person writes it, with any tagline cut off, or "your team" when that is still over 40 characters or six words. Nothing recites their metrics, no dash of any kind is sent (tools/draft_render cleans every inserted value and the whole email), and "We work in three areas", "If one fits, reply with its name", "I'd start with" and "18 things LCX can do" are gone. A lead the rules call not a buyer is never drafted; one held (Check service: a studio that sells what we would pitch, an answer of no_fit, a service picked only from its audience with nothing to confirm it) or found by Apollo with no site read (Read site first) is skipped and named in the draft log. The outreach row records the service it pitched (outreach.service, sql/35).

templates.subject: 18 things LCX can do for {{company}}
templates.guidance: The owner, 2026-10-08: "make a email structure for me that groq will follow". Five parts, top to bottom: (1) the greeting, as v1; (2) {{opener_block}}: ONE sentence the model writes about the company from what its own site says, a reason to buy now and the content accounts it runs, left out when there is nothing of theirs on record or the answer fails a check; (3) the owner's own lines from v1, word for word, with the deck attached; (4) {{pitch}}: one or two sentences the model writes naming two (at most three) of the services this lead's audience is pitched first, exactly as the deck names them, with what each would do for them -- or, when no model writes it, "I'd start with <first> and <second>."; (5) the owner's close and the footer, as v1. The subject is v1's. The model's leash is generated_pitch's (tools/llm.py LCXS_SYSTEM). A draft with model-written text is approved one at a time unless batch_approval.allow_generated says otherwise. Kept for the drafts written with it from 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-13; new drafts use v3, which the draft step picks first (the owner's review, 2026-10-13).

templates.guidance: The owner's choice, 2026-10-06: a short email with the services deck attached as a PDF, in the wording the owner approved. {{greeting_name}} is the person's first name when one is known, else 'there'. The deck in attachments goes with every email from this template; the sender checks it is the same file that was drafted and approved, and holds the email back if it changed. Kept for the drafts written with it before 2026-10-08; new drafts use v3, which the draft step picks first (v2 is kept for the drafts of 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-13).

templates.subject: Re: {{opener_subject}}
templates.guidance: The follow-up to the problem-first email: the one service it pitched ({{lead_service}}), the same ask (a few examples and a short note), the review's rules (Hello, never Hi there; no dashes; no claims).

follow_ups.guidance: Owner, 2026-10-23: "Make follo ups for all", after "set only 1 follow up after 4 days" for LCX Clipping. One follow-up, four days after the first email went out with no reply, in the same Gmail thread ("Re: <the first email's subject>"), from the same address, signed by the person whose Gmail the thread is in. It is a draft in the Follow-ups tab and needs approval like any email. Any reply stops it at once (an auto-reply lets it resume); Stop follow-ups ends the thread by hand; the database refuses one after a reply (sql/23).

batch_approval.guidance: Drafts may be approved together: select them in Drafts, read the random sample the server draws (at least sample_min, or sample_fraction of the batch, whichever is more), tick each, approve. Every draft is checked first (no {{placeholder}}, no SET_ME, a valid address, a sendable company, the deck present). A v3 draft whose problem and solution lines a model wrote is approved one at a time (allow_generated false); one that uses service_copy's fixed lines (no model) can still go in a batch, since a sample of them stands for the rest.

outreach.guidance: The owner, 2026-10-06: one email with the services deck attached, to the businesses the weekly harvest finds; since the owner's review of 2026-10-13, that email pitches ONE service, the lead's lead service, problem first (template lcx_services_problem_v3). Like US Production Houses: a shortlisted lead with an address is drafted by itself, a person approves it (one at a time, or a spot-checked batch), and it goes from that person's own Gmail (send_from approver, linked by the owner with tools/users.py gmail), inside that address's daily limit, which it shares with every other project. One first email per company and per inbox; no follow-ups. Not paused: the owner chose 'send once approved'. Replies land in Outreach -> Replies. The service an email pitched is recorded on its outreach row (outreach.service), a record of what was sold to whom.

lead_service.guidance: One service per lead, using Apollo industry, keywords, description, company facts and buying signals, plus the company's own website evidence. Apollo fields are retained for both automatic and manual saves. Existing human choices are preserved. Wrong buyers are excluded first; VFX and animation suppliers are held before hiring signals are considered. Other rules then match in configured order. Live-action film and TV producers can receive AI VFX + Animation without Wikidata classes. Shop Display Videos, Reel Forge and Audiobooks require specific evidence instead of an audience-only fallback. Unknown or ambiguous needs are held for review. Routing never changes the clipping project.

sourcing.guidance: Owner decision 2026-10-19: all new leads and contacts come from Apollo. Existing project constraints, gates and scoring remain. Company websites and news verify already-known leads; they do not discover new ones. Clipping is exempt. Owner, 2026-10-23: a lead a person found on their own is the exception ("send custom mail to a lead that we find on our own, as in lead is not generated by software"): Leads -> Add a lead adds it by hand with source 'manual', and the address that person typed in (contacts source 'manual', verifier 'person') may be written to (sql/42, tools/manual_lead.py). Nothing automatic adds a manual lead.
